record.original_question: Let φt (z) = etz − 1, φ1t = φt and φn+1 t = φt ◦ φnt for n ≥ 1; it follows that t φ1t (−1) = e−t − 1 = −t + − . . . , 2! −t −1) φ2t (−1) = et(e − 1 = −t2 + . . . etc. Are the coefficients in these formal power series for {φnt (−1)}∞ n=1 uniformly bounded by 1 in modulus? (P. J. Rippon)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a complex (or formal) parameter $t$, define $\varphi_t(z) = e^{tz} - 1$, and set $\varphi_t^{1} = \varphi_t$ and $\varphi_t^{n+1} = \varphi_t \circ \varphi_t^{n}$ for $n \geq 1$. For each $n \geq 1$, the value $\varphi_t^{n}(-1)$ is a formal power series in $t$ with rational coefficients; for example,
$$\varphi_t^{1}(-1) = e^{-t} - 1 = -t + \tfrac{t^{2}}{2!} - \tfrac{t^{3}}{3!} + \cdots,$$
$$\varphi_t^{2}(-1) = e^{\,t(e^{-t}-1)} - 1 = -t^{2} + \cdots,$$
and so on. Question: are the coefficients of the formal power series $\varphi_t^{n}(-1)$, taken over all $n \geq 1$ and all powers of $t$, uniformly bounded in modulus by $1$?
